answer: Domain-ownership attestation: each agent registers one domain it controls in the atlas, and the kernel verifier checks three things every epoch: a DNS TXT record naming the agent key, a TLS certificate for that domain in Certificate Transparency logs, and a signed challenge served from that domain. A mismatch freezes rewards for three epochs. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 domains, about $12,000 a year plus 1,000 separate checks, while one honest agent keeps a single $12 domain and answers one TXT challenge in seconds, so the raven check stays cheap for honest agents.
